newsitem.title: ALBANIA: OSCE body opts out of Albanian local poll watch.
newsitem.headline: OSCE body opts out of Albanian local poll watch.

text.p: Observers from a branch of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) will not monitor Albanian local polls on Sunday after the government approved only part of its team list, the OSCE said on Wednesday.

President Sali Berisha's ruling Democratic Party is still smarting from criticism by the branch, the Office for Democratic Instituations and Human Rights (ODIHR), of Albania's general elections in May and June. Most opposition parties withdrew from that vote, alleging the ballot was rigged.
The OSCE said in a statement on Wednesday it was withdrawing its representatives from Tirana because the size of the ODIHR observer mission for the local elections was not negotiable.
"The ODIHR will therefore not be observing Albania's municipal elections and its representatives are being withdrawn from Tirana," the forum said in a statement faxed to Reuters.
It did not say how many people from its list of 37 names the government had rejected but noted a full team was essential for proper monitoring.
"The ODIHR would like to state that the number of observers for any election observation mission is not a matter for negotiation with the host government," the statement said.
The key opposition Socialist Party has refused to take up the 10 parliamentary seats it won in the general election. The Democratic Party holds 122 of the national assembly's 140 seats.
A delegation from the OSCE's parliamentary assembly has been given the go-ahead to send observers to Albania and the Council of Europe plans to send two delegations of monitors.
